lead: The densest and most community-minded part of Gràcia, with its own shopping axis and a festa major in September.
text: It was rural land on the edge of the municipality of Gràcia until, around 1860, its owners developed it; the name comes from Jeroni Grassot, one of them. It has its own shopping axis, Gràcia Nova, and holds its festa major in the first half of September.

With 55,948 inhabitants/km², it is the densest neighbourhood in Gràcia, which shows in a very lively street, with local shops and blocks of flats. It is home to La Sedeta, the former textile mill that operated from 1899 to 1976 and now houses a secondary school and a civic centre, and to the church of l'Immaculat Cor de Maria. It is an option for anyone who wants the Gràcia atmosphere with a sale price (5,031 €/m²) slightly below that of La Vila.
housing: Blocks of flats from different periods on straight streets, with more recent areas in Ca l'Alegre de Dalt.
places: Església de l'Immaculat Cor de Maria
